chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zurara from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Aban ibn Uthman said: He told us that Kathir, the seller of pistachios, said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying:

Noah heard the creaking of the ship on Al-Judi, so he feared for it, and he put his head out from the side of the ship, raised his hand, and pointed with his finger while saying: 'Rahman, Atqin,' and its interpretation is: 'O Lord, Do good.'
And indeed Noah (peace be upon him), when he boarded the ship, boarded it on the first day of Rajab, so he commanded those with him from the jinn and humans to fast that day.
He said: Whoever among you fasts it, the Fire will be distant from him by a year's journey.
And whoever fasts seven days from it, the seven gates of the Fire will be closed to him.
And whoever fasts eight days from it, the eight gates of the Gardens will be opened for him.
And whoever fasts ten days from it, his request will be granted.
And whoever fasts twenty-five days from it, it will be said to him: Resume the work, for you have been forgiven.
And whoever adds more, Allah will add more for him.

key_terms.أَبَانُ بْنُ عُثْمَانَ: A prominent narrator in Shia hadith literature
key_terms.رَجَب: The seventh month of the Islamic lunar calendar, known for fasting
key_terms.كَثِيرٌ بَيَّاعُ النَّوَى: Kathir, the seller of pistachios, a narrator

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards of fasting on the first day of Rajab according to Prophet Noah?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) is reported to have boarded the Ark on the first of Rajab, establishing a precedent for fasting that day to secure divine protection. The narration details specific spiritual rewards for fasting varying durations within Rajab, ranging from distance from Hellfire to complete forgiveness, reflecting the Shia tradition's emphasis on the virtue of this month.
